scenarios.title: Queue and verify a one-time report
scenarios.summary: Copy the current arrivals list into a report once, five minutes after submission, as Mira. Verify actual output after advancing virtual time.
scenarios.objective: The virtual UTC clock starts at 2026-10-29 10:00. As Mira, write and save /work/report-job.sh so that it copies the current /work/report-input into /work/report-output. Queue exactly one job five minutes after submission. Run through 10:06 UTC and verify the report. Leave the queue empty and preserve the peer note. Fresh checks use different arrivals lists: do not type the report contents directly.

concepts.title: A job is work saved for later
concepts.text: A script is a text file containing commands. Type in the file editor; Save updates the simulated file. at -f reads that saved file and queues a separate copy. A line beginning # is a comment. Open the assignment directly if you already know this.

concepts.title: Copy live input, then choose a time
concepts.text: cat reads a file. In cat /work/sample-input > /work/sample-report, > replaces the output with that text. Queuing does not run it. at -f /work/sample.sh now + 3 minutes requests one run three virtual minutes after submission; -t 202610291003 names an absolute UTC minute. Our simulator supports only the documented subset.

scenarios.title: Repair a captured job without losing live updates
scenarios.summary: A queued dispatch report contains an old label. Repair the script and captured variables, replace the old job, then include an input update made after submission.
scenarios.objective: As Devon, inspect the pending job and its captured source. Replace that job with exactly one job from /work/dispatch-job.sh, five minutes after submission, capturing LABEL=Final in the variables editor. The script must write the captured label plus a newline, then the live input, into /work/dispatch-output. After submission, update /work/dispatch-input to arrivals: 9 followed by a newline. Run through 10:06 UTC; the report must read Final then arrivals: 9 on separate lines. Leave no pending jobs and preserve the peer note. Editing the old source or variables alone does not update its captured job.

concepts.title: The queued copy is separate
concepts.text: at captures saved script text and variable values when you submit. Saving a repaired file or changing the variable editor afterward does not rewrite an older job. Inspect at -c ID, remove the stale job with atrm ID, and submit the corrected file.

concepts.title: Captured variables and live input differ
concepts.text: A variable is a named value. Put LABEL=Approved in the supplied variables editor as a name/value pair; do not type export into the queue command box. printf '%s\n' "$LABEL" prints that captured value: %s is the text slot; \n ends the line; double quotes keep the value together. Then cat /work/sample-input >> /work/sample-output appends the live file; >> preserves earlier output.

concepts.title: Retry without resetting everything
concepts.text: Files used by cat are read when the job actually runs, so a saved input update after submission should appear. If the result is wrong, inspect script, captured variables, live files and due time separately. Removal affects pending work, not effects of a job already completed.

scenarios.title: Retire an obsolete job and preserve another owner’s work
scenarios.summary: Investigate two owners’ pending work, cancel only the obsolete job, and leave one correct replacement queued without disturbing the peer.
scenarios.objective: Inspect the queue as root and as Nia. Remove Nia's obsolete job, preserve Pat's job2 exactly, and leave exactly one Nia replacement from /work/owner-job.sh scheduled five minutes after submission. The replacement must copy the live /work/owner-input into /work/owner-output. Do not advance the virtual clock: this handover delivers pending work. The complete queue must contain only Pat's unchanged job and Nia's tested replacement. Listing owners does not change filesystem permissions.

concepts.title: An ID names a job, not its owner
concepts.text: atq shows only the selected ordinary account’s pending jobs; root can list all supplied owners. at -l is an alias. Use the account picker to inspect both views. These simulated owner rules do not implement filesystem permissions, root impersonation or at.allow/deny.

concepts.title: Remove exactly the obsolete work
concepts.text: at -c ID inspects captured text. atrm ID or at -r ID removes that pending job; do not assume ID numbers from another attempt. Read the returned ID after submitting a replacement. A newly queued job gets a new ID, while Pat’s existing work must retain its original captured contents and time.

concepts.title: A pending handover still needs a real script
concepts.text: A queue can look correct while its script is wrong. Here Check runs independent deterministic samples against captured work without changing your actual clock or files. Retaining a job in the pending queue is intentional in this assignment; the simulator’s result list is not real at mail or spool output.

scenarios.title: Hand over an ordered two-job report
scenarios.summary: Replace an obsolete report with an ordered producer/consumer pair, prove both jobs completed correctly, and preserve a peer’s future job.
scenarios.objective: As Tess, retire the obsolete job while keeping Pat's future job2 unchanged. Prepare a producer from /work/handover-job.sh at +2 minutes that copies live /work/handover-input to /work/handover-stage. Prepare a consumer from /work/handover-summary.sh at +5 minutes, capturing TITLE=Evening, that writes that title, a newline and the staged contents to /work/handover-output. Run through 10:06 UTC. Verify both files, both captured jobs and the ordering; only Pat's job should remain queued. Preserve the peer note. Fresh checks vary both the input and the consumer's available stage contents.

concepts.title: Two jobs form a dependency
concepts.text: A producer writes a file; a later consumer reads it. Saving both scripts and submitting both jobs is necessary. Give the producer an earlier due time and inspect both IDs. This exercise orders jobs serially; real at does not guarantee a later job waits for a slow earlier job, so real production dependencies need stronger coordination.

concepts.title: Verify current output and independent behavior
concepts.text: After Run, inspect the stage and final report, then Check. Fresh samples use different input for each captured script and compare all supplied files, exit status and errors. Matching one visible report is insufficient: the consumer must actually read its stage file and the producer must read live input.

concepts.title: Keep unrelated work intact
concepts.text: Root can inspect all queue entries, but having that ability does not mean removing every job is safe. Preserve the peer’s future ID, source, variables and time. Jobs past due are eligible at the next simulated Run; merely looking at a queue or closing the app does not advance this clock.
